**SUBJECT: FORMAL APPEAL REGARDING APPLICATION #449-B (THE GRAND EXPANSION PROJECT)**

Dear Superintendent,

I am in receipt of your letter dated [Date], in which you purport to deny Application #449-B to commission the carving of my likeness into the granite facade of Mount Rushmore. I am writing to formally appeal this decision. Furthermore, I reject every premise, justification, and alleged "scientific assessment" outlined in your response. I concede absolutely nothing. 

First, I do not accept your assertion regarding the "structural integrity of the Harney Peak granite." Your geological engineers claim that the rock face lacks the stability to support a fifth visage of such monumental proportions. I categorically dismiss this. Granite is entirely subservient to human will. If Gutzon Borglum could dynamite heavily fractured rock to reveal the likeness of Theodore Roosevelt, modern blasting techniques are more than capable of accommodating my cheekbones. I will not entertain any further discussion regarding the alleged fragility of a mountain. 

Second, your reliance on "historical preservation" and the "completed artistic vision" of the original sculptor is fundamentally flawed. History is not a stagnant puddle to be fenced off by federal bureaucrats; it is a continuum. Borglum stopped at four faces because he died, not because the pantheon of greatness reached maximum capacity. The argument that the monument is "finished" is a bureaucratic fiction. It is visually lopsided, and my profile is the necessary aesthetic anchor required to balance Washington’s sheer volume. 

Third, I refuse to acknowledge your citations of the National Park Service Organic Act of 1916. You argue that your mandate is to conserve the scenery for the enjoyment of future generations. I submit that future generations will find no greater enjoyment than gazing upon my fifty-foot granite jawline illuminated by the South Dakota sun. My addition does not disrupt the scenery; it elevates it to its ultimate, realized potential. 

To be absolutely clear: I am not proposing a compromise. I will not accept a smaller carving. I will not accept a bronze plaque in the visitor center. I will not pivot this project to the Crazy Horse Memorial. My face belongs adjacent to Abraham Lincoln, facing southeast. 

Consider this letter my final exhaustion of administrative remedies. I expect a full reversal of your decision and the immediate issuance of the necessary blasting permits no later than ten business days from the receipt of this letter. I have already retained a team of Italian sculptors, and their visas expire in the spring. 

Govern yourself accordingly.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]  
Chief Visionary, Application #449-B
